newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bills drift, rate stability awaited.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bills drift, rate stability awaited.

text.p: Philippine treasury bills drifted in the secondary market on Thursday as the call money market continued to pull the cash, traders said.
Funds which would have normally gone into T-bills were drawn into the overnight market due to the overall higher levels, traders said.
"It is the same sentiment and it will remain that way until interest rates stabilise. People will not position on T-bills until then," one trader said.
Bids on 91-day bills ranged from 13.50 percent to 13.75 compared with 13.40 to 14 on Wednesday. Offers for the three-month maturities ranged from 12.95 to 13.25 versus the previous 13 to 13.20.
The average interbank call loan rate was slightly down at 25.03125 percent from 25.0625 as liquidity in the market meant Of 37 banks which participated in the market on Thursday, 26 were lenders.
